quizName: DMV Practice Test #3 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to handle differently while you are riding, what should you do?

options.text: Continue riding normally.
Pull over and check the tires.
Pull over and check the chain.
Pull over and check the windshield.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check the tires.
questions.explanation: A sudden change in handling may mean a tire has failed. If your motorcycle handles differently, pull over safely and check your tires.

questions.question: If stopping your motorcycle will take longer than usual, what should you do?

options.text: Stay farther away from the vehicle ahead.
Stay closer to the vehicle ahead.
Leave the road.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther away from the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Stay farther away from other vehicles on slippery surfaces. If it takes longer to stop, increase your following distance.

questions.question: Which fabric gives the most protection for motorcycle riders?

options.text: Leather
Denim
Polyester
Wool

questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants provide the best protection when riding.

questions.question: How does riding with a passenger affect a motorcycle?

options.text: Usually causes no difference in handling.
Is usually safe for beginning riders.
Can change how the motorcycle handles.
Is encouraged to help riders practice.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can change how the motorcycle handles.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to a motorcycle, which changes how it handles. Only experienced riders should carry passengers.

questions.question: Which type of clothing helps other drivers see you?

options.text: Dark-colored clothes
Clothes made from synthetic materials
Reflective clothes
A leather jacket

questions.explanation: Wear gear that helps other drivers see you. Bright, reflective clothing makes it easier for others to notice you on the road.

questions.question: What happens when you drink alcohol quickly?

options.text: More alcohol builds up in your body.
Alcohol leaves your body faster.
Alcohol has less effect on you.
You are less likely to be pulled over.

questions.correctAnswerText: More alcohol builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: Drinking quickly causes more alcohol to build up in your body. It is never safe to ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: How can you make night riding safer?

options.text: Night riding should be avoided.
Wear reflective clothing.
Night riding is unsafe because turn signals are hard to see.
Only ride at night in the city.

questions.explanation: Wear reflective materials when riding at night to make yourself more visible to other drivers.

questions.question: If you have been drinking alcohol, what should you do?

options.text: Ride if you feel okay after drinking.
Set a drinking limit so you can still ride safely.
Do not ride.
Do not worry about your riding if you feel fine.

questions.explanation: The best way to avoid riding under the influence is to not ride after drinking. Any amount of alcohol can affect your abilities.

questions.question: Can one alcoholic drink affect your riding?

options.text: Yes, it can affect your judgment and riding skills.
No, one drink usually has no effect.
It affects you but only for a short time.
It affects you but coffee can remove it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it can affect your judgment and riding skills.
questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect your judgment and riding skills. Only time allows your body to remove alcohol.

questions.question: A DOT-approved helmet must have all of the following except:

options.text: An outer shell that resists impact.
An inner liner that absorbs impact.
A chinstrap that keeps the helmet on.
Bright colors painted on the outside.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bright colors painted on the outside.
questions.explanation: A DOT-approved helmet must have an impact-resistant outer shell, an impact-absorbing inner liner, a comfort liner, and a chinstrap that holds it on. Bright colors are not required.

questions.question: Where should you find information about your specific motorcycle?

options.text: The owner's manual.
A general book about motorcycles.
Someone who has a different type of motorcycle.
A television show about motorcycle riding.

questions.explanation: Read the owner's manual before riding your motorcycle for the first time. This is especially important if you are riding a borrowed motorcycle.

questions.question: How should you check tire pressure?

options.text: Look at the tire to see if it looks right.
Use a tire gauge.
Squeeze the tire with your hand.
Compare it to another tire's height.

questions.explanation: Use a tire gauge to check pressure before every ride. A tire that is not fully inflated may still look fine, so looking at it is not enough.

questions.question: Which of these do you NOT need to check before riding?

options.text: The headlight works.
The oil level.
Both brakes work and the brake light turns on.
The paint has no scratches.

questions.explanation: Before riding, check tire pressure and condition, oil and fluid levels, and make sure headlights, taillights, signal lights, and brake lights all work.

questions.question: What should you NOT check on your tires before a ride?

options.text: Air pressure
Wear
Tread
Shininess

questions.explanation: Before each ride, check air pressure, tread, and general wear of your tires.

questions.question: What type of footwear should you wear when riding?

options.text: Shoes with long heels.
Shoes with long laces that hang out.
Shoes that cover your ankles.
Shoes made from thin material.

questions.explanation: Wear boots or shoes that are high and sturdy enough to cover and support your ankles. Heels should be short and laces should be tucked in so they don't catch on the motorcycle.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. What should you do?

options.text: Do not ride during the day.
Always wear bright clothing.
Ride on the shoulder away from traffic.
Always wear dark clothing.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Always wear bright clothing when riding so other drivers can see you, even during the day.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: When should you use your turn signal?

options.text: When you plan to speed up.
Only when there is heavy traffic.
Every time you plan to change lanes.
Only at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you plan to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Use your turn signal every time you turn or change lanes, even if no one appears to be around.

questions.question: Which brakes should you use when stopping?

options.text: Only the front brake.
Only the rear brake.
Both brakes.
Either one, but never both at once.

questions.explanation: Always use both brakes at the same time to stop. Using both brakes together is the most effective way to stop.

questions.question: How can you make yourself more visible to other drivers?

options.text: Add extra lights to your motorcycle.
Do not use your turn signal.
Wear dark clothing.
Wave at people.

questions.correctAnswerText: Add extra lights to your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: To increase visibility, wear bright or reflective clothing. Adding extra lights to your motorcycle, using turn signals, and flashing your brake light also help other drivers see you.

questions.question: A rectangular sign shows:

options.text: School crossing.
Railroad crossing.
Stop.
Speed limit.

questions.explanation: Rectangular signs are used for rules like speed limits. They have white backgrounds with black letters or symbols. You must follow what these signs say.

questions.question: If you wait one hour after each drink before riding:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for riding after drinking.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
Alcohol effects may still be present.
You will be safe if you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol effects may still be present.
questions.explanation: Your body processes about one drink per hour on average. However, alcohol can still build up in your system. This buildup can still hurt your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: Alcohol affects your riding ability:

options.text: Starting with the first drink.
Starting at half the legal limit.
Starting at the legal limit.
Only after multiple drinks.

questions.explanation: Even one drink can hurt your riding skills. You can be impaired well below the legal limit. Do not drink any alcohol before riding.

questions.question: Which is NOT important when choosing a motorcycle helmet?

options.text: It meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards.
It fits snugly around your whole head.
It has no cracks or loose padding.
It looks cool.

questions.explanation: Check that your helmet meets U.S. DOT standards, fits snugly around your entire head, and has no damage like cracks or loose padding. How it looks does not matter for safety.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Skip the jacket on warm days.
Always wear a jacket, even in warm weather.
Wear shorts when it is warm.
Not worry about long shoelaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always wear a jacket, even in warm weather.
questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket when riding, even on warm days. A jacket helps protect you and prevents dehydration. Also wear long pants and tuck in shoelaces so they do not catch on the motorcycle.
